text:
priya: FYI saw a sharp spike in audit events for tenant: acme-inc at ~17:20 UTC, ingestion backlog grew, and KMS requests started returning 5xx. throwing this here to coordinate mitigation and customer-facing messaging. cc @dan @sarah :eyes:

ingest-monitor: ALERT 1728456160 - audit_ingest_queue_length > 20k for shard-4 (tenant=acme-inc)

dan: ugh. any idea if KMS errors are the root or just causing retries to amplify backlog?

priya: KMS is intermittent; logs show 503s from kms-gateway and our client retried 3x. also noticed our per-tenant sharding pins many of acme's events to shard-4.

sarah: two angles: (1) stop retry storm for KMS errors (exponential backoff + circuit breaker) (2) shed or route lower-priority audit rows to slow-path / cheaper index to buy headroom.

lee: agree. we should also consider temporary dynamic shard reassign for heavy tenants. re-sharding live might be rough but we can route new writes to other shards without migrating hot ones immediately.

priya: thoughts on customer-facing validation? acme will expect full audit coverage; if we shed, we need to surface exactly what fields/events were deprioritized.

dan: propose short-term: 1) set KMS client circuit to fail-fast after 2 retries for 30s for affected shard; 2) enable lightweight dedupe+aggregation for non-authorization events (reduce event count); 3) emit audit_delivery.status=degraded to tenant telemetry so we can show a clear message.

priya: sounds reasonable. can we sketch the config changes?

lee: quick draft config snippet (can push as feature flag):
```
audit_ingest: 
  retry_policy: 
    max_retries: 2
    backoff_ms: 250
  circuit_breaker: 
    error_threshold: 0.05
    window_sec: 30
    open_for_sec: 30
  routing: 
    hot_tenant_shard_limit: 5000
    slow_path: index_type: "cold-audit-compact"
```

sarah: + add metric: audit.events.shed_count and audit.events.aggregated_count. also we need a brief runbook line for support to explain to customers which event types were aggregated (e.g., telemetry.ping, session-heartbeat) vs never-aggregated (authz.create, key.rotate).

priya: agreed. I'll draft a short status note for acme (clarify no authz events lost). dan, can you wire the telemetry flag and the dedupe aggregation?

dan: on it. will also flip circuit breaker for shard-4 and add a quick alert suppressor to avoid paging on noisy 5xx KMS flaps.

ops-bot: deploy request queued by @dan for branch: fix/audit-circuit-172845 - ETA 8m

priya: one more ask — we should estimate cost impact if we route 30% of events to cold index versus backlog processing. ops/finance ballpark?

lee: rough calc: cold indexing ~0.02$/1000 events vs hot index ~0.12$/1000 events. routing 30% of 200k spike events => ~60k * (0.02 - 0.12)/1000 = ~-$6. So it saves money short-term but increases retrieval cost. I'll put a note in the ticket.

priya: perfect. I'll post the customer note once dan confirms telemetry and s3 cold index route. thanks all :pray:
thread_summary: Spike in audit events for tenant acme-inc; KMS 5xx causing retries and backlog. Plan: circuit breaker for KMS client, route non-critical events to cold index, enable aggregation/dedupe, emit degraded telemetry flag, draft customer message.
